content.title: About
content.content: Steamed trout retains most of its nutrients, offering a delicate flavor and tender texture. It is a popular choice in diet-friendly cooking because no added fat is required for the steaming process.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Trout belongs to the salmon family and is commonly farmed in freshwater ponds.
Steaming preserves up to 90 % of B‑vitamins, which are easily destroyed by frying.
In the wild, trout feeds on insects and small fish, making it rich in omega‑3 fatty acids.
In Japan, steamed trout is often served with soy sauce and ginger as a cooked alternative to sashimi.
Trout can grow up to 1.5 kg, but commercial production usually harvests fish weighing 300–500 g.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Steamed trout provides EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Approximately 20 g of protein per 100 g helps maintain muscle mass.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B12, B6 and niacin aid metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Trout supplies selenium, phosphorus and potassium, important for immunity and bones.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Steamed trout contains about 120 kcal per 100 g, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to trout.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Wild trout can accumulate mercury and cadmium; choose reputable sources.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improper storage can lead to bacterial growth and food poisoning.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Steamed trout can be served whole, flaked into salads, added to soups, or used in sushi rolls. It pairs well with lemon, dill, olive oil, and light sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked trout refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
